label: copy-phase input n fed back as one of the first two echoed tokens (early in sequence)
explanation: Fires only in the copy phase, only when the fed-back input token is n (100% of activations have in_tok = n), and almost only at recall_idx 1 or 2, i.e. when n was original token 0 or 1 and is now being re-input. It is strongest at recall_idx 1, the step right after <DEL> where first_tok = n is echoed: 85% of the mass, top activations near 4.5, and short sequences (L = 4-5) give the largest values. At recall_idx 2 (orig(1) = n) it is weaker (about 0.1-0.2 of max). It falls off with sequence length and time: it is silent at t >= 11 and rare for L >= 8, which is why the t <= 9 condition helps. It never fires on n in the original phase, on <DEL>, or on any other token, and it is essentially silent on later copy steps (recall_idx >= 3).

issues: Most of the base claims hold. All activation is on in_tok = n in the copy phase, with none in the original phase or on <DEL>. recall_idx 1 holds 85.3% of the mass and recall_idx 2 holds 14.6%, while recall_idx 3 has 284 active steps (0.1% of mass). The test scores reproduce exactly: P 0.846, R 0.960, F1 0.899.

The t <= 9 cutoff is a crude stand-in for the real rule, which is a different sequence-length (L) cutoff for each echo position. Dev precision for copy-phase n at recall_idx 1, by L: 1.00 for L = 3-6, 0.999 for L = 7, 0.76 for L = 8, 0.22 for L = 9. At recall_idx 2: 0.49 for L = 3, 0.99 for L = 4, 0.99 for L = 5, 0.80 for L = 6, 0.15 for L = 7, 0.002 for L = 8, 0.0 for L = 9.

This leaves a systematic class of false positives. At recall_idx 2 with L = 7 (t = 9), the predicate is true but precision is only 0.15, about 2.3k false-positive steps per split. These make up most of the 3864 test false positives; every one of the top false-positive examples shown has the form 'x n ... <DEL> x *n*' at step 9 or step 8.

A second, smaller false-positive class: recall_idx 2 with L = 3, the last step of the sequence (to_go = 0), fires only 49% of the time. The missed activations are scattered noise: recall_idx 3 with orig(2) = n, and recall_idx 1 with L = 9 (t = 10), together about 0.5% of the mass.

The label's phrase 'early in sequence' hides the fact that the feature depends on L separately at each echo position. The echo of orig(0) = n survives up to L = 7-8, while the echo of orig(1) = n survives only for L = 4-6.
skeptic.revised_label: copy-phase input n echoed as original token 0 (for L <= 8) or original token 1 (for L = 4-6)
